definition: A reaction in which the products can react with each other to turn back into the original reactants, so the change runs in either direction. Indicated in equations by the double arrow symbol ⇌.
msAccepts: the reaction goes in both directions
msAvoids: calling any reaction with a forward step reversible

definition: Without water: describes a substance whose water of crystallisation has been removed, such as the white anhydrous copper(II) sulfate formed when blue crystals are heated gently.
msAccepts: white form of copper(II) sulfate after heating
msAvoids: omitting the link to hydrated crystals

definition: Water that is packed into a crystal's structure as part of the solid. Gentle heating drives it out — blue copper(II) sulfate crystals turn white as they lose theirs — and adding water restores it.
msAccepts: water built into the crystal lattice
lost on heating the hydrated crystal
restored when water is added back

definition: Breaking a substance down into simpler substances using heat alone. The dehydration's forward change — blue copper(II) sulfate crystals splitting into the anhydrous solid and water — is an example.
msAccepts: broken down by heat into simpler substances

definition: A container from which no substances are added to the reaction mixture and none escape, though heat may be given off or absorbed through the walls. Reversible reactions reach equilibrium only inside one.
msAccepts: nothing added or able to escape
heat can still pass in or out
msAvoids: claiming energy cannot cross the walls

definition: The state reached in a sealed container when the forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate, so the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant. Both reactions are still happening throughout.
msAccepts: forward and reverse reactions at the same rate
msAvoids: omitting either the rate half or the concentration half

definition: The left-to-right reaction of an equation as written — the direction running from reactants to products. In A ⇌ 2B the forward reaction converts A into B.
msAccepts: the direction the equation reads first
msAvoids: confusing it with the faster direction

definition: The right-to-left reaction of an equation as written — the direction running from products back to reactants. In A ⇌ 2B the reverse reaction converts B into A.
msAccepts: the opposite direction to the forward reaction
msAvoids: confusing it with the slower direction
saying it always absorbs exactly zero heat

definition: A statement of which side of the equation dominates the equilibrium mixture: it lies left when there is more reactant, right when there is more product. Changing conditions can shift it, altering the constant concentrations.
msAccepts: a shift changes the constant concentrations
msAvoids: treating position as a physical place
omitting that shifts respond to condition changes

definition: For two identical molecules to join together into one pair-molecule. Nitrogen dioxide dimerises to form dinitrogen tetroxide, the colour change behind the brown-to-pale equilibrium readout.
msAvoids: calling it a condensation of gas to liquid
omitting that the molecules are identical

definition: The amount of desired product obtained from a reaction. For a reversible reaction the yield is set by the position of equilibrium, so conditions that shift the position towards the product side raise it.
msAvoids: saying a catalyst raises the yield
